title: Weakly supervised causal skill routing with role-specific relational encoders
coverage_gap: Only paired low/low and high/high layouts occur in N10. An unconstrained joint representation can couple where to grasp to where to insert, and can conflate closing, lifting and inserting because their relative hand/peg offsets are similar. Independent peg/box shifts require reusing skills without assuming the demonstrated timing or y correlation.
reusable_regularity: Learn four soft representation branches for approach, contact/closing, transport and insertion. Approach/contact branches see peg-relative hand geometry rather than goal coordinates; transport/insertion branches see the pegHead-to-goal error and grasp contact. A causal router is trained with weak stage annotations made from support gripper/z commands and measured head height. At deployment it predicts solely from geometry, aperture and motion, without labels or a time clock. The DP consumes all soft-gated branches, a world-context encoder, an ungated metric safety skip and router logits (124 features per observation). Gates never prescribe native actions or plan a path.
dependencies_preserved: all branches use signed world coordinates; reach and transport roles separate peg placement from goal placement
a 0.025 per-branch routing floor prevents any geometry branch from being completely discarded
the ungated grasp gap and pegHead-to-goal error keep robot/object/box relations accessible through stage uncertainty

an always-on world encoder receives absolute hand/goal, current orientation, orientation difference and hand/object motion, retaining finite-workspace, fixed box orientation and robot dependencies rather than claiming global translation or rotation symmetry
gripper aperture, gripper change, measured object movement and absolute heights distinguish approach, contact and carrying
the head-to-grasp offset remains explicit in transport encoders; the two sites are never substituted for one another
evidence_refs: bundle.json: ten current-support episode IDs, no development data or expert source
task_materials.json: LL/HH support, independent factor definitions, shared raw observation and native action semantics
support_summary.json: five support episodes per training cell; nonconstant gripper aperture and large vertical motion across demonstrations

images/frame_02_demo_01_step_034.png: descending hand aligned over the peg, not yet inserting
images/frame_03_demo_01_step_091.png and images/frame_06_demo_03_step_079.png: raised peg at the side opening

trajectories/demo_00.json: actions[0:16] initially open with z positive then negative; actions[32:64] positive gripper with downward contact commands followed by upward/lateral transfer; obs[48:54] shows changing aperture and object movement
trajectories/demo_01.json: obs[34:37] shows approach/closing geometry while the head is still near table height
contracts.py and learning.py: learned modules registered in build_modules, training-only target path, valid-mask auxiliary normalization
expected_failure_signature: The key falsifiable risk is routing error under extrapolation: contact may be predicted too early before a secure grasp, or the transport branch may persist after height alignment. This would produce grasp misses or repeated rise/descend transitions despite reasonable initial reaching. Weak labels are not physical stage or success oracles; the 0.03 m height band can label a laterally misaligned peg as insertion, so large transverse E offsets may still cause premature insertion. Small N may also overfit the learned world branch. No performance claim is made.

required_runtime_fields.omitted: Declared absent object2 zero fields only. No runtime stage, demonstration ID, reset factors, episode time, future state or action, or success label.
required_runtime_fields.action_frame: Identity world action4 encode/decode. XYZ remains native 0.01 m-per-unit world translation; the gripper coordinate is unchanged. No clipping or execution override exists in the candidate.

training_only_targets.name: skill_stage
training_only_targets.shape: [windows,2], aligned to the two causal history timestamps, including repeated initial observation
training_only_targets.source_fields: Only this D_N: actions[u,3], actions[u,2], obs[u,41] (pegHead z), obs[u,38] (goal z), with u=max(0,t-1) or t
training_only_targets.definition: 0 if gripper command is negative; otherwise 1 if head is more than 0.03 m below goal and z command is nonpositive; otherwise 2 if still below that band; otherwise 3. These are weak skill labels, not evaluator stages or success thresholds.
training_only_targets.loss: 0.05 times cross-entropy of the causal router, separately normalized by mask[:,0].sum()*2. All class labels are on valid history points. Public action epsilon loss stays weight 1 and denominator mask.sum()*4.
training_only_targets.inference_isolation: Labels exist only in training_targets/training_loss. condition uses measured raw_history, and denoise exposes its router logits for the training loss. No teacher stage is concatenated at inference or training.

support_fit: No fitted statistics, persistent episode cache or auxiliary pretraining. Learned encoders and router are registered in build_modules and optimized only jointly in the common fixed updates.
change_summary: Initial pre-feedback design with learned soft skill routing, four role-specific bounded MLP encoders, an always-on world encoder and a weak stage cross-entropy auxiliary. Unlike the deterministic contact-chain candidate, representation specialization is learned and stage-supervised. Common DP backbone and world action4 are unchanged.
